meta.title: The Ice That Was Thinner
meta.skill_frame: Argument and evidence: find the claim, the reason, and the fact behind the reason.

reader.who: Older students who read at about a third-grade level.
reader.why_this_level: The load is one claim and one rule as the reason, so a number settles the question. Measured FK 3.45 and 3.40 on the two parts (60 and 49 words), 3.43 together. The reading sits inside the grade 2-3 band and below the 4.1 floor, which measures 5.3 at its easiest.
reader.tone: Adult subject. Plain sentences. The lesson must not make the reader feel small.

source.attribution: Original text drafted for argument_evidence 3.1, band 3.1, sequence 2. No external work.
source.text_status: Drafted for the band, accepted on spot check.
source.survey: A pond group that closes a gate, built so the claim is stated, the rule is the reason, and the measurement is the evidence.
source.avoided: No pond name, town, or dates. No claim about the weather.

session.difficulty_basis: One claim and one rule as the reason; the reader must see that a number, not an opinion, settles it.

authoring_exceptions: Parts run 45-60 words instead of 100-200. At band 3.1 the text is short by design: two parts keep the session inside 12 minutes and the claim, reason, and evidence stay visible on one screen. Recorded under 2.1.

script_overrides.near_copy_2: Say it in your own words. One sentence is enough.

passage.part_1: A pond group checks the ice every winter. They cut a hole near the middle of the pond and measure the ice with a ruler. In past years the ice was seven inches thick in January. This January it measured four. The group wrote a short note for the town. The note says the pond is not ready for skating.
passage.part_2: The note gives a reason. The club rule says ice must be six inches thick before a crowd may stand on it. Four inches holds one person, not thirty. The group will measure again next week. Until the ice reaches six inches, the gate at the pond stays closed.

items.prompt: What does the group's note ask the town to accept?

tutor_only.confirm: Right. The pond is not ready for skating.
tutor_only.correct_reason: The last sentence of the first part gives the claim: the pond is not ready for skating.
tutor_only.tell: The claim closes the part about the ice check. The pond is not ready for skating.
help: Look at the last sentence about the ice check.
The sentence says what the pond is not ready for.
tutor_only.core_idea: The pond is not ready for skating.
accept_ideas: the pond is not safe to skate on
the ice is too thin for skating
tutor_only.normalize: Ignore case, punctuation, and minor spelling. Accept a meaning-preserving paraphrase.

if_they_say.when: the student says the ice is four inches
if_they_say.ask: Four inches is the measurement. What does the note say the town should accept?

items.prompt: Why is four inches not enough for a crowd?

tutor_only.confirm: Yes. The club rule needs six inches for a crowd.
tutor_only.correct_reason: The passage says the club rule requires six inches before a crowd may stand on the ice.
tutor_only.tell: The club rule sets six inches for a crowd. Four inches holds one person, so a crowd cannot stand on it.
help: Find the sentence about the club rule.
The rule gives a number for a crowd.
tutor_only.core_idea: The club rule needs six inches of ice before a crowd may stand on it.
accept_ideas: the rule says six inches are needed for a crowd
six inches are needed for a crowd
four inches only holds one person, not thirty
tutor_only.normalize: Ignore case, punctuation, and minor spelling. Accept a meaning-preserving paraphrase.

if_they_say.when: the student says four is a small number
if_they_say.ask: The passage gives a rule with a number. What number does the rule ask for?

items.prompt: How does the group know the ice is thinner than in past years?

tutor_only.confirm: Right. They measured it with a ruler both years.
tutor_only.correct_reason: The passage gives seven inches in past years and four inches this January, both from the same check.
tutor_only.tell: The group cuts a hole and measures with a ruler every winter. That is how it has seven inches for past years and four for this one.
help: Look at the sentence that names the ruler.
The passage gives two numbers for the same check.
tutor_only.core_idea: They measured the ice with a ruler and compared this year with past years.
accept_ideas: they measured the ice with a ruler
they cut a hole and used a ruler
seven inches before and four now
tutor_only.normalize: Ignore case, punctuation, and minor spelling. Accept a meaning-preserving paraphrase.

if_they_say.when: the student says because it was cold
if_they_say.ask: The passage does not talk about the weather. It talks about a measurement.

items.prompt: A reader says the pond never freezes now. Does the note report that?

tutor_only.confirm: No. It reports thinner ice, not ice that never forms.
tutor_only.correct_reason: The passage reports four inches this January, so the pond did freeze.
tutor_only.tell: The pond froze this January. The note reports four inches of ice, which is thinner than seven, not ice that never forms.
help: Find the sentence with this year's measurement.
It gives a number of inches.
tutor_only.core_idea: No. The pond froze four inches thick this January.
accept_ideas: no, there were four inches of ice
no, the ice is thinner but it did freeze
tutor_only.normalize: Ignore case, punctuation, and minor spelling. Accept a meaning-preserving paraphrase.

if_they_say.when: the student says yes because the gate is closed
if_they_say.ask: A closed gate is the response, not the report. How thick was the ice this January?

items.prompt: The note gives the club rule instead of asking people to be careful. Why does it do that?

tutor_only.confirm: Right. The rule gives the number that settles it.
tutor_only.correct_reason: The rule states six inches, so the reader can compare it with the four inches the group measured.
tutor_only.tell: The rule gives a number the town can compare with the measurement. Careful skating has no number, so the rule does the work.
help: Look at the number in the rule and the number in the measurement.
One is six and one is four.
tutor_only.core_idea: The rule gives a number that can be checked against the measurement.
accept_ideas: so the town can compare numbers
the rule sets six inches and the ice is four
a rule is stronger than a warning
tutor_only.normalize: Ignore case, punctuation, and minor spelling. Accept a meaning-preserving paraphrase.

if_they_say.when: the student says rules are always better
if_they_say.ask: The passage uses one rule and one number. What does the number let the town do?
